current.meaning: "Whatever ya spend over and above that, I'll pay ya back when I come back." preserves the repayment promise; all framing questions, the love command, contrasted passers-by, injuries, care, animal, inn and two denarii remain in order.
current.sense: "his heart went out to him." correctly expresses compassion; put him to the test, bashed, cleared off and over and above also retain their intended senses.
current.authenticity: "They stripped him, bashed him and cleared off," is coherent broad Australian narration, consistent with the speaker throughout.
current.register: "There was a cove headin' down from Jerusalem to Jericho" sustains broad vocabulary and cadence alongside ya, yer and everyday paraphrases, without adding prohibited garnish.
current.tone: "The one who showed him mercy." keeps compassion and the serious moral point central, with no trivialising joke about the violence.
current.flow: "A Levite did the same: he got to the spot, saw him and went past on the other side." moves the narrative clearly and naturally aloud.
current.variety: "his heart went out to him." adds a different idiom from getting to his feet, clearing off, looking after him and paying back, without repetitive tags.
current.essence: "But the lawyer wanted to justify himself," preserves the framing motive, followed by the same illustrative narrative and final moral command.

engine.meaning: "what will I do to inherit eternal life?" makes the opening question predictive rather than clearly asking what is required; the narrative and practical details otherwise survive.
engine.sense: "You'll love the Lord yer God hand on heart" misuses hand on heart, which conveys sincerity or truthfulness rather than loving with the whole heart.
engine.authenticity: "Who's me neighbour?" uses plausible Australian speech forms, as do ya reckon and gave em; the amount of retelling is assessed under register.
engine.register: "Behold, a certain lawyer stood up and tested him, saying," retains the original biblical body cadence, representative of much eligible narration; scattered pronouns and elisions fall well short of level 5.
engine.tone: "He who showed mercy on him." preserves the serious moral concern; the violence and compassion are not turned into jokes.
engine.flow: "when he came to the place'n saw him" jams a reduced conjunction into otherwise formal syntax; the similar him-and join makes this a repeated interruption to reading aloud.
engine.variety: "do ya reckon" offers a different form from cove, yer and gave em, without repeated added openers or tags.
engine.essence: "Go and do likewise." retains the final moral imperative, with the framing challenge and contrasting neighbourly actions still recognisable in the same narrative shape.

engine.quote: what will I do to inherit eternal life?
engine.original: what shall I do to inherit eternal life?
engine.why: Meaning: will asks about a future action rather than clearly asking what the speaker must do, weakening the question that initiates the teaching.

engine.quote: You'll love the Lord yer God hand on heart
engine.original: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart
engine.why: Sense: hand on heart is an assertion of sincerity or truthfulness. It does not mean with the entirety of the heart, so it misrenders wholehearted devotion.

engine.quote: Behold, a certain lawyer stood up and tested him, saying,
engine.original: Behold, a certain lawyer stood up and tested him, saying,
engine.why: Register: substantial eligible biblical phrasing remains with sparse substitutions. This contract permits rewriting both speech and narration and asks for sustained level-5 voice without added garnish.

engine.quote: when he came to the place'n saw him
engine.original: when he came to the place and saw him
engine.why: Flow: the reduced conjunction is glued to place inside retained formal syntax; the similar join after him causes another jarring interruption.

summaries.current: A coherent broad Australian retelling preserving the parable, its details and serious moral purpose.
summaries.engine: The serious parable remains, but a wrong idiom, altered opening question, light voice and clumsy joins weaken it.
